      ],
      "description": "{\"scope\": [\"Reuse def-b-spline-space-and-basis including its Cox-de Boor recurrence, zero-denominator and endpoint conventions. Define ONLY de Boor coefficient evaluation (distinct from evaluating all basis functions), returning value on a specified nonempty knot span with p-degree loop and range/rounding status.\", \"Reuse thm-spline-polynomial-reproduction for support, partition of unity, nonnegativity, basis and derivative facts.       "items": [],
      "scaffold": "research/plan-numerical-linear-track.md",
      "order": 2560
    }

    "statement": "Let $F\\in\\{\\mathbb R,\\mathbb C\\}$, $A\\in F^{n\\times n}$, $B\\in F^{n\\times m}$, $C\\in F^{p\\times n}$, and $R=R^*\\in F^{m\\times m}$ be positive definite. Write $Q=C^*C$ and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. The inverse $R^{-1}$ is well-defined: [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]] supplies an invertible factor $R=LL^*$, so $R^{-1}=L^{-*}L^{-1}$. Thus $v^*Gv=\\|L^{-1}B^*v\\|_2^2\\ge0$ and $v^*Qv=\\|Cv\\|_2^2\\ge0$. The symbol $^*$ is transpose over $\\mathbb R$ and conjugate transpose over $\\mathbb C$.\n\nThe **continuous algebraic Riccati equation (CARE)** is\n$$A^*X+XA-XGX+Q=0.$$\nIts residual is $F_c(X)=A^*X+XA-XGX+Q$, its feedback is $K_c(X)=R^{-1}B^*X$, and its closed-loop matrix is $A_c(X)=A-BK_c(X)=A-GX$.\n\nFor $X=X^*\\succeq0$, $S_X:=R+B^*XB$ is positive definite because\n$v^*S_Xv=v^*Rv+(Bv)^*X(Bv)>0$ for every nonzero $v$. The **discrete\nalgebraic Riccati equation (DARE)** is\n$$X=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA.$$\nIts residual is $F_d(X)=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA-X$. Whenever $X=X^*$, the matrix $R+B^*XB$ is positive definite if $X\\succeq0$. Its feedback and closed-loop matrix are\n$$K_d(X)=(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA,\\qquad A_c(X)=A-BK_d(X).$$\nA CARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian and $A_c(X)$ is Hurwitz. A DARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian, $R+B^*XB\\succ0$, and $A_c(X)$ is Schur stable. No inverse of $A$ is part of either definition.\n\nFor Hermitian $X$ with $S_X$ invertible, multiplication gives\n$$(I+GX)^{-1}=I-BS_X^{-1}B^*X,\\qquad X(I+GX)^{-1}=X-XB S_X^{-1}B^*X.$$\nIn either product, the additional coefficient of $B$ is\n$R^{-1}-S_X^{-1}-S_X^{-1}(B^*XB)R^{-1}=0$, because\n$S_X=R+B^*XB$.     "statement": "In the dense arithmetic model, a single-matrix Schur reduction or regular-pair QZ reduction of order $n$ with at most $s$ Francis/QZ sweeps has core work $O(n^3+sn^2)$: the initial Hessenberg or Hessenberg-triangular reduction costs $O(n^3)$ and each full bulge-chasing sweep costs $O(n^2)$. Forming a graph candidate by solving $XU_1=U_2$ with dense $n\\times n$ factorization, $n$ right-hand sides, and residual multiplication costs $O(n^3)$.\n\nAfter an order-$d$ reduction, finite stable-block reordering with $k$ actual attempts costs $O(d^2+kd)$ scalar operations. If the form has $b$ diagonal blocks and $I$ complementary-before-selected inversions, then $I\\le b(b-1)/2$; successful ordering requires $K\\ge I$ and enough scalar/evaluator budget $W$ for the entire execution, including validation, label and inversion scans, all $I$ swaps, and the final ordering scan. For a Riccati pencil or Hamiltonian with $d=2n$, successful reordering, graph solve and equation-level residual multiplication preserve the $O(n^3+sn^2)$ scalar-core bound. This exact postprocessing count excludes algebraic bit cost, evaluator implementation cost beyond its declared unit budget, dense product-factor evaluation, local residual-ball certificate production or validation beyond the charged dense operations, and any additional dense residual multiplication.           "statement": "Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\\subset\\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable set, let $M:=|D|$, let $q\\in L^\\infty(D;\\mathbb C)$, and let $k\\in\\mathbb R$. Here $L^2$ and $L^\\infty$ are equivalence classes modulo null functions ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), and $L^\\infty$ means essentially bounded with respect to Lebesgue measure ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]). We regard $q$ as zero off $D$. The convention is the volume equation\n$$u=f+K_k u,\\qquad K_k u(x):=\\int_D G_k(x-y)q(y)u(y)\\,dy,\\qquad G_k(z):=\\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\\pi|z|}\\quad(z\\ne0).$$\nSet $G_k(0):=0$; when $M>0$ the diagonal in $D\\times D$ is product-null, so this value is only a representative convention. The input and unknown are classes in complex $L^2(D)$, and the displayed equation is interpreted as an equality of those classes. Its formula is well defined by [[lem-volume-integral-operator-well-defined-and-bounded]].\n\nThe associated far-field map is\n$$\\mathcal F_k[v](\\theta):=\\frac1{4\\pi}\\int_D e^{-ik\\theta\\cdot y}q(y)v(y)\\,dy,\\qquad \\theta\\in S^2.$$\nHere $S^2$ has the surface measure of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. The map is well defined as a continuous function of $\\theta$ by [[lem-volume-far-field-map-is-bounded]].\n\nFor $x\\notin\\overline D$, the exterior volume potential is\n$$V_kv(x):=\\int_D G_k(x-y)q(y)v(y)\\,dy.$$\nFor each $v\\in L^2(D;\\mathbb C)$, the essential-supremum result gives $|q|\\le\\|q\\|_\\infty$ almost everywhere, and Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\\|qv\\|_{L^1(D)}\\le\\|q\\|_\\infty\\sqrt M\\,\\|v\\|_2$.           "statement": "Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Use the unit sphere $S^2$ and its polar surface measure $d\\sigma$ from [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]].
